english_head: SIMPLE colours are the proper colours of the elements, i.e. of fire, air, water, and earth. Air and water when pure are by nature white, fire (and the sun) yellow, and earth is naturally white. The variety of hues which earth assumes is due to coloration by tincture, as is shown by the fact that ashes turn white when the moisture that tinged them is burnt out. english_head:
Air seen close at hand appears to have no colour, for it is so rare that it yields and gives passage to the denser rays of light, which thus shines through it; but when seen in a deep mass it looks practically dark blue. This again is the result of its rarity, for where light fails the air lets darkness through.
When densified, air is, like water, the whitest of things.
